widget.prompt: A semicircle of radius 6 spins about its diameter, sweeping a sphere. Set the radius and read the volume as a multiple of π.
widget.successFeedback: 288π. The sweep is what makes it a sphere: every point of the semicircle traces a circle, and (4/3)π(6³) = (4/3)(216)π = 288π. Revolution is not a new formula — it is where the formula comes from.
widget.lowFeedback: Smaller than the swept sphere. The semicircle has radius 6, so grow the radius toward it.
widget.highFeedback: Larger than the swept sphere. The semicircle has radius 6, so bring the radius back down.

commonBuilds.feedback: 36π is the sphere of radius 3 — half the radius gives an eighth of the volume, not half. Cubing is what makes the difference so large.
144π would be (2/3)π(6³), the hemisphere the semicircle sweeps only if it stopped halfway. A full spin about the diameter sweeps the whole sphere: 288π.

refusals.title: The Sphere Surrenders
refusals.why: REFUSAL REASON CORRECTED. S203K said 'no engine represents a sphere as manipulable state' — that was false; volumeBuilder has solid: sphere. The real reason stands: this step asks WHICH THREE earlier results justify the sphere formula, a synthesis question about the structure of a proof, not a quantity anyone can build.
